The kernel passes. Both compilation and correctness checks are green, and it's faster than the PyTorch reference.

**Results summary:**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Compiled | yes |
| Correctness | 5/5 trials |

The implementation uses a straightforward per-element approach: each thread handles one output position, iterates over the 4x4 kernel window, and computes the max in FP32 before storing back as BF16. Even without shared-memory tiling, the kernel beats the reference thanks to the spatial locality giving good L2 cache hit rates at stride=1.
